questions.prompt: What is the standard decorator function signature in TypeScript 5.0+?

options.text: (value, context) — the decorated value plus a context object describing it

questions.explanation: Standard ECMAScript decorators receive (value, context). The (target, key, descriptor) shape belongs to the older legacy decorators.

questions.prompt: Do standard decorators require a compiler flag?

options.text: No — standard decorators work out of the box in TypeScript 5.0+; the legacy ones require experimentalDecorators

questions.explanation: Standard decorators need no flag in TS 5.0+. The older legacy decorators require the experimentalDecorators option.

questions.prompt: Which can standard decorators decorate? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Standard decorators apply to classes, methods, getters/setters, fields, and auto-accessors — but not parameters, which are legacy-only.

options.text: Registers a function to run during instance (or class) initialization — useful for binding methods or registering instances

questions.explanation: addInitializer schedules setup code to run at initialization time, e.g. to bind a method to this per instance.

questions.prompt: Legacy decorators require the ______ compiler option. (the option name)
questions.explanation: The legacy decorator implementation is enabled with experimentalDecorators and uses the older signature.

questions.prompt: If a method decorator should change behavior, what must it do?

options.text: Return a replacement function; returning nothing leaves the original method unchanged

questions.explanation: A method/class decorator that transforms behavior returns the new function/class. Returning void leaves the original in place.
